purpose: Corrects the interpretation of the operational persistence versus no-contraction comparison. Numerical D3 results are unchanged; this document only states what the existing intervals do and do not support.
reason_no_further_testing: The paired intervals D3 already produced answer the question. Running another test on the same development sample would be a second look at data already used, and would search for a conclusive result rather than measure one.
conclusion: On macro MAE, persistence and no-contraction are effectively tied within uncertainty at both horizons. The preregistered tie-break on high-stress false negatives resolves the selection decisively in favour of persistence, and the selected benchmark is unchanged.
why_persistence_is_not_weak: An inconclusive MAE difference is not evidence of a weak benchmark. Persistence is selected on two grounds: a lower point-estimate macro MAE at both horizons, and substantially fewer high-stress false negatives under the registered tie-break (8 vs 21 at h=1; 4 vs 28 at h=3). Missing a high-stress event is the costly error for an early-warning system, and no-contraction never predicts one at all.

future_model_comparator_policy.note: Future models must beat the selected persistence baseline as the primary comparator and must also report no-contraction as a secondary comparator. No-contraction is retained precisely because it is close on MAE.
